why_difficult: Not difficult by design -- a clean, uncomplicated 4-page text-only PDF (standard font, single column, no images) with clearly distinguishable per-page content, included as a baseline/control fixture so ground-truth expectations have a 'nothing should go wrong here' reference point.

license: Public domain -- Neil M. Judd, "Archeological Investigations at Paragonah, Utah" (Smithsonian Miscellaneous Collections, Vol. 70, No. 3), published 1919 by the Smithsonian Institution; Internet Archive item metadata records possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT and no access restriction. Vendored file is a locally-trimmed subset (pages 2-32 of the original 52-page IA derivative PDF, re-saved with pikepdf to drop unreferenced objects) to stay under the corpus size cap; sha256 above is of the trimmed file actually committed, not IA's original derivative.
why_difficult: Genuine Internet Archive OCR scan with a PARTIAL text layer: 22 consecutive pages of dense real body text (running headers alternating 'ARCHEOLOGICAL INVESTIGATIONS AT PARAGONAH-JUDD' / 'SMITHSONIAN MISCELLANEOUS COLLECTIONS VOL. 70' with page-number folios) are bracketed by front-matter pages with ~0 extracted characters (bookplate, blank flyleaves, duplicated title-page scans) and end in a full-page rotated line-drawing site plate with 0 extracted text -- the positive real-world case for defect D (an extractor must not choke on or hallucinate text for a genuine image-only page) and defect A (running headers/folios must be recognized, not swallowed into body text).

license: Public domain -- Lewis Carroll (1832-1898), "Alice's Adventures in Wonderland", first published 1865; this scanned printing is a ca. 1910 Tenniel-illustrated edition. Internet Archive item metadata (identifier alicesadventures0000lewi_i4x4) records no access restriction. Vendored file is a locally-trimmed 12-page subset (original pages 13-24, re-saved with pikepdf/new-document page copy to drop unreferenced objects) to stay well under the corpus size cap; sha256 above is of the trimmed file actually committed, not IA's original derivative.
why_difficult: Genuine Internet Archive scan of a typeset novel spanning Chapter I's opening ('DOWN THE RABBIT-HOLE.') into the start of Chapter II, chosen for dense quoted first-person dialogue in ordinary book typography (positive case for defect F: prose dialogue must never be misdetected as a code block) and a real chapter heading plus an alternating running header/folio that must survive extraction (defect E).

license: Public domain -- Project Gutenberg eBook #23500, C. N. and A. M. Williamson, "The Car of Destiny", first published 1908. Project Gutenberg only distributes texts confirmed public domain in the United States.
why_difficult: Not difficult by design -- NEGATIVE CONTROL fixture: a clean, well-formed, born-digital PDF (Project Gutenberg's own generated PDF, vector text, no scan artifacts) trimmed to 12 pages (title page, table of contents, and the Chapter I / Chapter II openings) containing plenty of quoted dialogue and real chapter headings, included so that any defect guard (A/D/E/F) firing here is known to be a false positive.
